content: There is no death, only a change of sacred worlds.
author: Native American Proverbs
explanation: To view death as a terrifying annihilation is the product of materialist blindness. In the sacred wisdom of the earth, the caterpillar does not die; it becomes a winged moth. The drop of rain does not perish; it joins the vast ocean. Spirit simply sheds its worn winter coat.
practicalInsight: Release the grip of existential dread today. Rest in the timeless continuity of sacred consciousness.
reflectionPrompt: How would your daily peace deepen if you viewed physical death not as an end, but as a sacred transition?
